advances: Ordinary planar geometry, explicit bump chart, full missing corner area and an actual marked point. The long edge fraction need not tend to zero.

proof:
Write $b=1+h/(1-k)$. On the edge joining $be_1,e_2$ the point at fraction $k$ from $be_1$ is $(1-k)be_1+ke_2=(1+h-k,k)$. The point $e_1$ cuts the other incident edge at fraction $(b-1)/b=h/(1+h-k)$ from $be_1$. Their joining line removes the indicated corner, and the cut fractions $r_1=h/(1+h-k)$ and $r_2=k$ give its area fraction $\tau=r_1r_2$. They obey $r_1\le2h/(1+h)<1/100$, $r_2<51/100$ and $\tau\le h\le1/10000$. In the specified barycentrics the removed corner is, up to its null boundary, the triangle $u/r_1+v/r_2\le1$ with $u=\lambda_1\ge0$, $v=\lambda_2\ge0$. For nested uniform laws the signed density changes sign exactly at the smaller body, and its negative part has mass $\tau$. Thus total variation in the convention $\sup_E|\mu_Q(E)-\mu_S(E)|$ equals $\tau$, and the removed-corner halfspace attains this value among halfspaces.

Write $\Gamma=4/9$. The stated mark $y$ is in the barycentric window of the low-cap localization lemma and is inside $Q$ since all its coordinates are positive and its first neighbor coordinate exceeds $r_1$. Any through-$y$ cap of $S$ of area fraction at most $\Gamma+1/10000$ is of vertex type with coefficients in $(29/20,31/20)$ by that lemma. A vertex-$0$ cap can lose at most $\tau|S|$. A vertex-$1$ cap misses the removed corner, because on it the cap's left side is at least $(29/20)(1-u)>1$. A vertex-$2$ cap can intersect the removed corner only where
$$
v\ge1-1/A_0+(A_1/A_0-1)u\ge9/29-1/1550>3/10.
$$
The relative fraction of the corner above that threshold is at most $(1-(3/10)/r_2)_+^2\le49/289<1/5$. Thus the three loss bounds relative to $|S|$ are $(\tau,0,\tau/5)$.

For a vertex-$i$ cap through $y$, the constraint $A_j\lambda_j(y)+A_k\lambda_k(y)=1$ gives $1/(A_jA_k)\ge4\lambda_j(y)\lambda_k(y)$ by AM–GM. Subtract the corresponding loss bound and substitute the stated barycentrics. The three lower bounds relative to $|S|$ are
$$
\Gamma-2\tau/5+9\tau^2/50,\quad
\Gamma-2\tau/5-27\tau^2/100,\quad
\Gamma-2\tau/5-27\tau^2/50 .
$$
Every other through-$y$ cap of $S$ loses at most $\tau$ in that normalization and started above $\Gamma+1/10000$, so its retained fraction is at least $\Gamma$. Every containing halfspace contains its parallel through-$y$ halfspace. Divide the smallest bound by $1-\tau$. After subtracting $\Gamma$ and comparing with $\tau/45$, the remaining numerator over $1-\tau$ is $\tau(10-233\tau)/450\ge0$.
statement: Let $Q=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,e_2,(1+h-k,k))$ with $0<h\le1/10000$ and $0<k\le(1+h)/2$. The triangle $S=\operatorname{conv}(0,[1+h/(1-k)]e_1,e_2)$ contains $Q$ and its missing corner has relative area $\tau=hk/(1+h-k)$ and incident cut fractions $h/(1+h-k)$ and $k$. With $\mu_Q,\mu_S$ the uniform probability measures, their halfspace-cap distance and total variation both equal $\tau$. In $S$-barycentric coordinates labeled with the removed vertex first and its short and long edge neighbors next, the point with coordinates $(1/3-9\tau/20,\,1/3+3\tau/10,\,1/3+3\tau/20)$ lies in $\operatorname{int}Q$ and every closed halfspace containing it has $Q$-probability at least $(4/9-2\tau/5-27\tau^2/50)/(1-\tau)$. In particular the maximum normalized ordinary halfspace depth satisfies $D(Q)-4/9\ge\tau/45$.
title: Linear ordinary depth excess for a small quadrilateral bump
